subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sara Lee <sara.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Alex / Sara - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so everyone has the same view, plus a recommended set of next steps. I've attached a cost model (acme_tco_modeling.xlsx) and a short pricing summary.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Per-call latency needs: 90th percentile < 400ms for user-facing chat.
- Bursty traffic (weekday peak 2-3x baseline) with strict budget cap from Finance (target <$8k/month for the pilot).
- Concern about token-driven costs as usage scales (current usage ~5M tokens/month; expected to grow).

Goals we discussed:
- Pilot to validate user engagement at ~10k DAU with a capped monthly spend.
- Preserve output quality (no aggressive quantization that changes responses) while optimizing unit economics.
- Simple procurement path (one PO + SOW) and a 30-60 day timeline for pilot.

TCO & cost levers (high level, see attached workbook for math):
- Current baseline (hosted API w/ standard model): ~5M tokens/month -> estimated compute cost ~$2,000/mo (using $0.0004/token effective rate).
- Projected at scale (20M tokens/month) -> ~$8,000/mo if no optimizations applied.
- Batching & concurrency: enabling continuous request batching on your typical request distribution reduces per-token compute by ~15-25% (depends on latency SLOs).
- Prefix/KV caching: for chat flows with repeated context, enabling prefix caching can reduce generation tokens by ~20-35% for many of your common flows (we highlighted examples in the workbook).
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated) + quantization profile: moving to a Dedicated pool with int8/4 quantization profiles can reduce unit costs further (~30-40%) but requires a 3-6 month committed contract.

Recommended pilot configuration to hit your < $8k/mo constraint while meeting latency targets:
1) Start on Redwood Hosted with medium-size model variant + continuous batching enabled (we can tune batching windows in week 1).
2) Turn on prefix caching for the top 10 conversation templates we discussed (we'll share the JSON rules).
3) Use guardrails on max output tokens (90-120 tokens typical) to limit tail costs.
4) Parallel track a Dedicated capacity quote (Rafael can provide numbers) if you decide to commit after pilot.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Marissa: Send finalized TCO workbook + sample caching rules (today) - attached.
- Alex: Share 1) top 10 conversation templates, 2) procurement contacts and PO cadence (by EOD Tue).
- Rafael: Provide Dedicated pricing and estimated latency SLOs for the recommended pool (by Tue COB).
- Neha: Schedule a 30-minute tuning session with your engineering team to validate batching settings (suggest Wed afternoon).

Questions / open items:
- Any constraints on data residency or encryption beyond standard SOC2/KMS? (you mentioned Finance may request additional audit logs)

Thanks - I'll follow up with the workbook and a short Loom that walks through the assumptions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: acme_tco_modeling.xlsx (workbook), redwood_pricing_summary.pdf (summary)

Thanks Marissa - this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) The Finance target is actually $7.5k/mo for the pilot (including any third-party hosting). Can the baseline plan be tuned to that number?
2) For caching: good to know ~20-35% savings. Can you call out the risk of increased staleness (i.e., when we need fresh responses) and how Redwood handles cache invalidation?
3) Procurement: I'll loop in our procurement lead, Sara, once I confirm the PO cadence - target to get that to you by Tue.

Also - Sara's on this thread for procurement and security questions. Appreciate Rafael and Neha joining the tuning call.

On the numbers, I'd like to see a conservative scenario in the workbook that assumes only 15% batching savings and 20% caching savings. If that still fits under $7.5k for the pilot, we're comfortable moving forward.

Alex

Alex - thanks for the cadence. A couple of notes from the pricing/ops side: 

- I'll prepare a Dedicated capacity quote that includes a reserved pool sized for your projected 20M tokens/month. That quote will show three options: 1) Pay-as-you-go Hosted (no commitment), 2) 3-month committed burst pool, 3) 12-month reserved capacity. Each option will include estimated monthly unit costs and the expected latency at 90th percentile.
- For the pilot (goal <$7.5k): based on Marissa's workbook, the conservative savings scenario (15% batching + 20% caching) still projects about $6.9k/mo at 20M tokens, and ~$2.2k/mo at your current 5M tokens. If you target the pilot volume closer to 12-15M tokens, you'll land in the $4.5-5.5k range with the conservative assumptions.
- Cache invalidation: Redwood supports per-route TTLs and explicit invalidation APIs. For chat use cases where freshness matters, we recommend short TTLs (30-120s) for dynamic routes or an explicit 'no-cache' flag on specific messages. Our SDK exposes these controls so engineers can mix cached vs. fresh generation per request.

I'll attach the Dedicated quote and a short latency breakdown in the shared Drive link; Rafael will follow up with a DocuSign-ready SOW if you want to move straight to reserved capacity after pilot.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
